page.introduction.002: One language for all of SteamProfiler.
page.introduction.003: Tokens, components and small details. The same visual foundation for the site, Duo and everything that comes next.
page.introduction.004: Built from the same pieces#
page.introduction.005: Panels that organize, numbers that tell a story and one amber accent. The examples in this documentation use the library's actual CSS.
page.introduction.012: Load the fonts and the compiled file. The classes work on any HTML page, with no required JavaScript.
page.introduction.013: A few rules, one consistent foundation#
page.introduction.015: Prefixed classes, shared tokens and React components that write the same HTML.
page.introduction.017: Override the page tokens. Every component follows the palette.
page.introduction.019: Use the primary button for the main action and tones to communicate state.
nav.002: The previews use the library's real components.
page.installation.002: A CSS library, with an optional layer of React components.
page.installation.004: The project distributes copies to neighboring fronts. Build the CSS and sync from the UI checkout.
page.installation.005: Sync writes to site/ui.css, next/src/ui-kit/ and Duo's src/ui-kit/. Also copy fonts/ if the project does not have the fonts yet.
page.installation.007: Include the library CSS before the front's own styles. Use the classes directly in HTML.
page.installation.009: The wrappers require React 19 or later. Import the CSS once and use the components from the local copy.
page.installation.011: In a front with layered styles, import the library into the components layer. Utilities can then adjust spacing and size.
page.installation.013: The checks verify types, class and component parity, and the copies in consumers.
page.tokens.003: Color, typography and density. The names that connect every component.
page.tokens.005: Amber marks the main action. Closely related surfaces leave room for content.
page.tokens.008: A palette for each page#
page.tokens.009: Tokens have no prefix to preserve the names used by the fronts. A themed page overrides the same variables.
page.tokens.011: Adjust an instance with CSS properties without creating a new variant.
page.typography.002: Bricolage Grotesque for headings. Archivo for reading. IBM Plex Mono for data and labels.
page.typography.004: Use the hierarchy without changing the element's meaning. Display accepts the as property.
page.typography.007: One rectangle per game. An area proportional to the hours you played.
page.typography.009: The amber square and wordmark follow the page colors.
page.typography.011: The heading uses the library's default size. A CSS property changes the instance's scale.
page.buttons.003: Clear actions, with a variant for each level of importance.
page.buttons.005: Reserve primary for the main action. Quiet supports it; danger indicates deletion.
page.buttons.007: Three sizes for actions in content, bars or forms.
page.buttons.009: The native disabled attribute disables interaction. For a toggle, expose its state with aria-pressed.
page.buttons.011: The element's native properties are also accepted.
page.buttons.018: The same variants on a link
page.panels.002: The shared container: a title bar, an action and room for content.
page.panels.005: The games that are part of your story.
page.panels.007: Use tight for lists, images and content with its own spacing.
page.panels.009: PanelGo with external opens a new tab and adds the arrow. PanelAction renders a button.
page.panels.011: Content to the right of the title
page.pills.002: Rounded links for navigation and small controls in bars.
page.pills.005: Marks the active link or button
page.chips.002: Compact filters that change content within a panel.
page.chips.004: Click the preview to change the filter. The application must control the state.
page.chips.007: Updates the filter in the application
page.tags.002: Small labels for categories and states, with semantic tones.
page.tags.004: A tag communicates a state. Include text so the information does not rely on color alone.
page.segmented.002: Two or three options that change a panel's purpose.
page.segmented.003: One choice at a time#
page.segmented.004: Click the options. Each button exposes its selected state.
page.forms.002: Native fields, labels associated with controls and help close to the content.
page.forms.005: The profile needs Game details set to public.
page.forms.007: The menu is native to the browser. The pill variant fits in a navigation bar.
page.forms.014: Receives the id to associate the control
page.notices.002: Feedback for errors, confirmations and states close to the content.
page.notices.004: Messages enter the queue one at a time.
page.notices.005: Received. Your message is in the queue.
page.notices.007: That profile does not exist or Steam did not respond.
page.notices.009: Notice uses role="alert" by default for the bad tone. In plain HTML, add the attribute explicitly.
page.stats.002: A highlighted value and a label explaining what it represents.
page.rows.002: A list of links with a small supporting value before the title.
page.skeleton.002: A placeholder for text that is still on its way.
page.skeleton.004: The visual element is hidden from assistive technologies. Indicate loading on the container with aria-busy.
page.skeleton.006: The animation is disabled when the visitor prefers reduced motion. The placeholder remains visible.
